your_book:
Friday, August 14 was a mixed but broadly resilient session for Jaleel's book, which sits on an unrealized gain of 6.74% overall. The damage was concentrated in a handful of names: Broadcom (AVGO) was the sharpest loser at –5.93% on the day, though at roughly 1.5% of the book the portfolio-level impact was contained. Zoetis (ZTS) fell –2.7%, ServiceNow (NOW) –2.55%, Adobe (ADBE) –2.39%, and Vertex (VRTX) –2.07% — tech and high-multiple software were clearly under pressure even as the headline on NOW's session included an analyst defending the software sector against AI-displacement fears. On the positive side, Neurocrine Biosciences (NBIX) added +1.26%, Boston Scientific (BSX) +0.27%, and the book's largest single weight, Rocket Lab (RKLB, 15.8%), was nearly flat at +0.19%.

The drift worth flagging is the divergence between ratings and price action in two places. ZTS carries a STRONG BUY and a QARP of 84.6 — the highest quality score in the book — yet it's down –6.3% in total and fell nearly 3% today; thesis and price are moving in opposite directions, which is either an opportunity or an early signal that the thesis needs retesting. Similarly, LULU sits on a –6.5% unrealized loss with a BUY verdict, but the guidance-cut flag (Americas comps –5%, fifth straight quarter) is a structural concern the rating hasn't fully absorbed. RKLB remains the elephant: a 15.8% weight — by far the largest position — rated AVOID with a QARP of just 36.6 and only a 2.4% gain to show for it.

Watch NVDA into August 26 (next catalyst), where export-control headlines and AI-capex sentiment can swing the chip complex quickly. ADBE's session headline was modestly positive — a Workday M&A rumor lifting peers — but the AI-narrative overhang and CFO exit remain unresolved heading into the September 10 report. The pharma cluster (GILD, NVS, NBIX, VRTX) carries a standing MFN/tariff policy flag that hasn't moved today but doesn't go away.

attention.headline: Largest weight, lowest quality — AVOID rating unresolved
attention.note: At 15.8% of the book, RKLB is nearly 6 points heavier than the next largest holding, yet it carries an AVOID verdict and a QARP of 36.6 — the weakest score in the portfolio — creating a significant concentration risk that contradicts Jaleel's capital-preservation mandate.

attention.headline: –5.93% single-session drop on a HOLD-QUAL name
attention.note: Broadcom's near-6% selloff today is the steepest single-day move in the book; with a HOLD-QUAL verdict and a QARP of only 64.9, the session warrants checking whether a specific catalyst (earnings, export-control news, or index rebalancing) drove the move before treating it as noise.

attention.headline: Highest QARP in the book, but –6.3% unrealized and falling
attention.note: Zoetis's STRONG BUY / QARP 84.6 thesis is diverging sharply from its price trend — down another 2.7% today and –6.3% overall — warranting a fresh check on whether the fundamental case remains intact or the market is seeing something the model isn't.

attention.headline: Guidance-cut flag active; –6.5% unrealized on a BUY-rated name
attention.note: With Americas comps negative for a fifth straight quarter, tariff margin pressure, and a stalled China business, the BUY verdict and the deteriorating fundamentals are in tension — the September 2 catalyst date is the next moment to reassess whether the rating still holds.
